stem: A toddler with a broad flat nose and prominent epicanthal folds appears cross-eyed to the family, but the eye examination is otherwise normal, what is the most likely explanation?

options.text: Pseudostrabismus can occur in some children with these facial features
This appearance confirms a neurological disorder
This pattern is typical of chemical conjunctivitis
These features make urgent ED referral mandatory even if no other concerns are present
These facial features exclude true strabismus permanently

explanation: Pseudostrabismus is the most likely explanation. Broad flat nasal bridge and prominent epicanthal folds can create the appearance of eye misalignment even when the eyes are actually aligned.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Strabismus

rationale: Correct because broad flat noses and epicanthal folds can make a child appear cross-eyed despite normal alignment on examination.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because broad flat noses and prominent epicanthal folds can create the appearance of misalignment, producing pseudostrabismus.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because this appearance alone does not confirm a neurological disorder.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because chemical conjunctivitis does not present as pseudostrabismus from facial anatomy.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because urgent referral depends on associated red flags and examination findings, not these facial features alone.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because these facial features can mimic strabismus but do not permanently exclude true strabismus.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
